title: David Fincher Describes Mindhunter's Grueling 90-Hour Workweeks
excerpt:
The director revisited the intense production demands behind Netflix's crime series.
High costs and unexpected showrunning duties help explain the absence of a third season.
body_md:
David Fincher has revisited the difficult production of Netflix's Mindhunter, according to a report by The Playlist. The account describes workweeks reaching approximately ninety hours, major production challenges and an unusually demanding level of responsibility for the filmmaker.

Fincher reportedly did not originally intend to serve as the series' showrunner. He ultimately found himself taking on that responsibility, adding ongoing operational decisions to the creative demands of a detailed crime drama. The report portrays the production as exhausting for the people involved.

Mindhunter developed a devoted audience through its patient exploration of criminal psychology and interviews with serial killers. Its creative reputation, however, did not resolve the financial problem identified in the report: the series was expensive to make, and its viewership was not sufficient to justify those costs.

That tension helps explain why a third season never materialized. The source does not present these comments as a new renewal announcement, nor does the feed excerpt contain a fresh production plan. It is a retrospective account of the obstacles that prevented the show from continuing.

The excerpt does not provide a detailed budget breakdown or the full interview transcript, so specific production figures beyond the reported ninety-hour workweeks should not be invented.

For fans, the remarks underline a difficult reality of ambitious television: artistic recognition and audience enthusiasm do not necessarily outweigh the combined pressures of scheduling, staffing, leadership and production economics.
